name: Freetown
subtitle: Freetown, capital of Sierra Leone: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 1,055,964 people live in the Western Area Urban district (Freetown) (counted 2015).
Freetown City Council describes Freetown as Sierra Leone's capital, principal port, commercial hub and largest city.
Freetown City Council says the city is home to over a million people, 40% of Sierra Leone's urban population.

parts.text: Freetown City Council describes Freetown as Sierra Leone's capital, principal port, commercial hub and largest city.
Freetown City Council says the city is home to over a million people, 40% of Sierra Leone's urban population.
Philanthropists founded the 'Province of Freedom' in 1787; it later became Freetown.
About 1,200 freed Black settlers, later known as the Nova Scotians, travelled from Halifax to Sierra Leone by ship in 1792.
Britain set up a naval base at Freetown to patrol against illegal slave ships.
By 1855 more than 50,000 freed slaves had been settled in Freetown.
Krio, a lingua franca, is the default language of communication in Sierra Leone, particularly in the major cities including Freetown.
The Sierra Leone Ports Authority says Freetown has probably the finest natural harbour, being sheltered, in West Africa.
Sierra Leone's main seaport, the Queen Elizabeth II Quay, is in the east end of Freetown at Clinetown and has 7 berths.
Fourah Bay College, founded in Freetown in 1827, was the first Western-style university on the West African coast.
Freetown City Council reports planting and tracking 1.2 million trees against its 1 million trees target (#FreetownTheTreeTown).

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in the Western Area Urban district (Freetown)?

parts.text: 1,055,964 in 2015, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Western Area Urban district (the Freetown urban area) in the 2015 census; the provisional 2021 mid-term census figure of 606,701 was publicly disputed and is not used.

items.text: British philanthropists founded the 'Province of Freedom', which later became Freetown.
About 1,200 freed settlers from Nova Scotia travelled by ship from Halifax to Sierra Leone.
The colony officially became a British Crown Colony.
Fourah Bay College was established, the first Western-style university on the West African coast.
Construction of the original Fourah Bay College building began in Cline Town under its first principal, Edward Jones.
By this year more than 50,000 freed slaves had been settled in Freetown.
The Sierra Leone National Museum was established as the museum of the Sierra Leone Society.
The effects of the Civil War in 1999 and a fire shortly afterward left the Old Fourah Bay College building in poor condition.
The national census counted 1,055,964 people in Western Area Urban.
The Cotton Tree, a national symbol, was felled in a storm.
Gola Rainforest National Park and Tiwai Island, as the Gola-Tiwai Complex, were named a UNESCO World Heritage site, Sierra Leone's first.
